title: Sparse Data, Known Equation
situation: You have few measurements, but a trusted equation and boundary or starting information exist.
why: The equation can check the fitted field where measurements are missing.
use_if: the equation is trusted
the scientific job is one specific field or case
boundary or starting information can be stated
avoid_if: the equation is incomplete
the hard regions are not checked
the claim needs a full input-to-output field map
evidence_needed: held-out measurements, boundary checks, equation residual checks, and comparison against a trusted solve when possible

decision_burden.shortage: measurements may be sparse, but the answer must still respect a known physical equation
decision_burden.observed: some measured values, boundary values, starting values, and a known differential equation
decision_burden.hidden: the full field value at every point in space and time
decision_burden.move: fit a neural network while also measuring how badly its output violates the known equation
decision_burden.carries: the model is not allowed to match points while freely breaking the equation between those points
decision_burden.rejection: move the training points, inspect sharp regions, and compare against a numerical solve or held-out measurements

title: Many Related Simulations
situation: You have many solved examples and need fast answers for new inputs from the same family.
why: The useful object is the map from input fields to output fields, not one solved field.
use_if: the input family can be named
many trusted input-output field pairs exist
new queries stay inside the tested family
avoid_if: only one problem instance exists
the training family is vague
new boundaries or grids are assumed rather than tested
evidence_needed: held-out fields, changed resolution tests, boundary tests, and checks on the scientific output quantity

decision_burden.shortage: one simulation answer is not enough when engineers need the whole map from inputs to solution fields
decision_burden.observed: many example inputs and their full solution fields
decision_burden.hidden: the rule that maps a new input field to its new solution field
decision_burden.move: learn the map from problem input to solution, not only one solution at a time
decision_burden.carries: the learned object is a shortcut for a family of solves, so the family must be named
decision_burden.rejection: change resolution, coefficients, boundary conditions, or forcing and check whether the predicted field still satisfies the scientific quantity being claimed

title: Expensive Repeated Decisions
situation: A trusted solver or experiment is too slow for design, search, control, or uncertainty sweeps.
why: A fast stand-in can answer repeated questions if its use range is stated and checked.
use_if: the slow trusted source is named
the repeated query family is narrow enough to test
the decision quantity is explicit
avoid_if: speed is the only evidence
the query family keeps changing
edge cases are not compared against the trusted source
evidence_needed: full-solver comparisons near the edge of use, decision-metric error, and a stated use range

decision_burden.shortage: a trusted simulator may be too slow to run for every design, control, or uncertainty question
decision_burden.observed: expensive solver inputs and outputs for a limited set of cases
decision_burden.hidden: the solver answer for every new query someone wants to ask
decision_burden.move: train a cheaper stand-in for the expensive input-output behavior
decision_burden.carries: speed is useful only inside the query family where the stand-in was checked
decision_burden.rejection: compare against the full solver on new cases near the edge of the intended use

title: Need A Readable Law
situation: Prediction is not enough; the output should be a formula or mechanism people can inspect.
best_start: Symbolic regression or neural differential equations
why: The scientific product is a candidate rule, not only a number returned by a fitted model.
use_if: important variables are measured
a changed experiment is available
a compact rule would be useful for science
avoid_if: key variables are missing
the formula is selected only on original data
the allowed ingredients cannot express the system's behavior
evidence_needed: changed-experiment tests, missing-variable checks, noise checks, and scientific inspection of the selected rule

decision_burden.shortage: a scientist may need a readable equation, not only a model that predicts well
decision_burden.observed: measured variables and candidate mathematical ingredients
decision_burden.hidden: which short formula, if any, actually explains the measured change
decision_burden.move: search for a readable equation that fits the data and survives a changed case
decision_burden.carries: a compact equation is a claim about structure, rather than only a curve through points
decision_burden.rejection: remove a needed variable, add noise, or test a new experiment and see whether the formula still predicts

title: New Setting Risk
situation: A model trained in one setting is being used in another setting.
why: The main question is whether the prediction should be believed under the change.
use_if: the changed condition can be named
the decision cost of being wrong matters
held-out or shifted tests can be built
avoid_if: only familiar tests are available
the error measure does not match the decision
confidence is reported without a use range
evidence_needed: changed-case tests, use-range statements, error on the decision quantity, and first-failure examples

decision_burden.shortage: a prediction is not enough unless the user knows when it should be believed
decision_burden.observed: training cases, validation cases, prediction errors, and known shifts between cases
decision_burden.hidden: how wrong the model may be on a case unlike the ones it learned from
decision_burden.move: separate fit on familiar examples from evidence on changed examples
decision_burden.carries: a prediction without a use range is not yet a scientific claim
decision_burden.rejection: move one important condition outside the training range and measure the first failure

title: Broad PDE Coverage
situation: One model is proposed for many equations, grids, parameters, or scientific tasks.
why: The claim is about shared structure across tasks, so whole task families must be tested.
use_if: many task families exist
shared structure is plausible
whole families can be held out
avoid_if: the new task is only assumed to be covered
rare regimes are missing
scale is treated as proof of scientific trust
evidence_needed: held-out task-family tests, trusted-solver comparisons, boundary and scale tests, and failure reports

decision_burden.shortage: one trained model may be asked to handle many related equations, grids, parameters, or physical settings
decision_burden.observed: many PDE problem instances across equations, grids, parameters, or physical settings
decision_burden.hidden: which shared structure carries from one scientific task to another
decision_burden.move: train one broad model to reuse structure across many related field-prediction tasks
decision_burden.carries: breadth is useful only if the new task shares the structure the model actually learned
decision_burden.rejection: hold out a new equation family, boundary type, scale, or rare regime and compare against a trusted solver

title: Many Examples, No Clear Rule
situation: You have many examples, but no trusted equation or readable law yet.
why: The first useful move is to learn a flexible predictor, then test whether it carries the quantity that matters.
use_if: examples are plentiful
the measurement process is named
a held-out changed case can be built
avoid_if: the new setting differs from the examples
the target quantity is vague
a scientific rule is claimed without a rule check
evidence_needed: held-out examples, changed measurement tests, target-quantity error, and a named first failure

decision_burden.shortage: scientists often have examples of behavior but no short rule that predicts the next case
decision_burden.observed: many input-output examples from experiments, simulations, or measurements
decision_burden.hidden: the exact rule that connects the input to the output
decision_burden.move: adjust many weights until the model maps familiar inputs to the right outputs
decision_burden.carries: the model earns attention only when prediction survives examples it did not train on
decision_burden.rejection: hold out a changed material, geometry, parameter range, or sensor condition

title: Scientific Claim Needs Discipline
situation: A model is being called scientific, but the claim, evidence, and failure boundary are not yet separated.
why: The field-level job is to make the learned answer answerable to evidence, physical quantities, and changed cases.
use_if: the scientific quantity can be named
the evidence source is visible
the failure boundary matters for a decision
avoid_if: the page only names a method
generic accuracy is treated as scientific proof
the domain limit is missing
evidence_needed: source anchors, a named scientific quantity, domain-specific checks, and a changed-case rejection test

decision_burden.shortage: scientific work needs predictions that respect measurements, equations, uncertainty, and domain limits at the same time
decision_burden.observed: data, equations, units, simulation outputs, and domain limits
decision_burden.hidden: which parts of the scientific system are missing, noisy, or too costly to compute directly
decision_burden.move: combine learned prediction with scientific checks that name what the claim is allowed to mean
decision_burden.carries: the model is judged by a scientific job, not by a score floating away from the job
decision_burden.rejection: state the scientific quantity first, then test it under a changed case that matters in that domain

title: Training Score Burden
situation: A model improves a written score, but the scientific decision may depend on something the score ignored.
why: Training only improves what the objective asks it to improve, so the objective must match the scientific burden.
use_if: loss terms are visible
the ignored requirements can be listed
post-training checks are possible
avoid_if: the loss is treated as the decision
rare cases or boundaries are not scored
the optimization target hides units or constraints
evidence_needed: loss-term inspection, ignored-requirement tests, held-out edge cases, and the decision quantity after training

decision_burden.shortage: learning needs a way to decide which model settings are better or worse
decision_burden.observed: a written score that says which model behavior is better or worse
decision_burden.hidden: whether that score matches the scientific behavior the user actually cares about
decision_burden.move: change model settings to lower the written score
decision_burden.carries: the model learns the score, so the score must include the scientific burden
decision_burden.rejection: inspect what the score ignores, then check whether the ignored behavior fails after training

title: Need Many Valid Possibilities
situation: The task needs many candidate fields, molecules, designs, or futures rather than one answer.
why: The useful product is a set of possible scientific objects that still obey the rules that matter.
use_if: many plausible candidates are useful
validity checks can be stated
downstream use can reject bad samples
avoid_if: samples are judged only by appearance
constraints are not checked
rare but important cases are missing
evidence_needed: constraint checks, rare-event checks, downstream-task tests, and examples of rejected samples

decision_burden.shortage: some tasks need many possible examples, not one predicted answer
decision_burden.observed: examples of fields, molecules, flows, shapes, or other scientific objects
decision_burden.hidden: the spread of possible valid objects beyond the examples
decision_burden.move: learn how to sample new candidates that resemble the training family
decision_burden.carries: a generated object must still pass physics and usefulness checks
decision_burden.rejection: measure constraints, rare cases, conservation, and downstream task performance on generated samples

title: Connected Object Matters
situation: The object is a molecule, mesh, graph, surface, or network where connections carry part of the scientific meaning.
why: Flattening the object can hide which parts influence which other parts.
use_if: nodes, edges, distances, or geometry matter
symmetries or mesh changes can be tested
the target property depends on interactions
avoid_if: the chosen graph is arbitrary
long-range effects are missing
rotation or mesh changes break the claim
evidence_needed: mesh-change tests, symmetry checks, missing-interaction tests, and target-property error on changed objects

decision_burden.shortage: many scientific objects are not simple rows of numbers; their connections matter
decision_burden.observed: objects with parts and connections, such as meshes, molecules, or interacting components
decision_burden.hidden: which neighboring and long-range interactions control the scientific quantity
decision_burden.move: let information move along the object connections instead of flattening the object into a plain row
decision_burden.carries: the model keeps the structure of the scientific object visible
decision_burden.rejection: change the mesh, rotate or move the object, or add missing interactions and inspect what breaks

title: Far Field Information Matters
situation: A local part of a scientific field depends on distant regions, but carrying every interaction is expensive.
why: Attention gives a way to route selected information across a field while making the routing choice testable.
use_if: nonlocal effects are plausible
the routing or window choice can be varied
the scientific quantity depends on distant context
avoid_if: attention is treated as explanation by itself
long-range effects are not stress tested
window choices are fixed without evidence
evidence_needed: window-change tests, long-range interaction tests, boundary-stress cases, and error on the scientific quantity

decision_burden.shortage: a local patch of a field may depend on faraway information, but looking everywhere can be expensive
decision_burden.observed: large fields where one location may depend on other locations
decision_burden.hidden: which distant parts matter for the local prediction
decision_burden.move: let the model choose which parts of the field exchange information
decision_burden.carries: attention is a routing rule for information, not proof that the selected route is physically complete
decision_burden.rejection: change the window size, inspect long-range effects, and compare behavior near boundaries or sharp structures

title: Field Rule Before Method
situation: A quantity changes across space, time, or both, and one number cannot describe the scientific state.
why: The PDE names how local change, movement, sources, and boundaries must fit together before a learned method is trusted.
use_if: the field quantity is named
boundaries or sources matter
conservation or stability can be checked
avoid_if: points are predicted independently
boundary conditions are unknown
the equation is incomplete for the experiment
evidence_needed: boundary tests, source-term checks, conservation or stability checks, and changed-grid or changed-scale cases

decision_burden.shortage: a quantity changes over space and time, so one number is not enough to describe the situation
decision_burden.observed: a field such as temperature, pressure, concentration, velocity, or displacement
decision_burden.hidden: how every point in the field affects nearby points over time
decision_burden.move: write a local change rule that uses rates across space and time
decision_burden.carries: the equation carries how a whole field changes, rather than only how one number changes
decision_burden.rejection: change the boundary, grid, source term, or physical scale and check conservation, stability, and measured error
